<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1105
Claimant:
Christine Yoder
Adjuster:
Darin Tyler
June 23, 2024
Claim opened after the policyholder reported a low-speed collision while backing out of a space in a parking lot. The
claimant's vehicle was the other car involved, and the claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact goes
through the attorney's office.
June 25, 2024
Reviewed the statement from the policyholder, who confirms the impact occurred as described when backing out.
The driver is a household member living with the policyholder and is covered under the policy as such.
June 27, 2024
Obtained photographs of both vehicles and the parking area. The damage on the claimant's vehicle lines up with the
impact the policyholder described.
July 25, 2024
Spoke with two witnesses who saw the collision from a nearby walkway. Both independently described the same
sequence of events the policyholder gave.
October 20, 2024
Contacted the other driver, who gave an account consistent with the policyholder's version. No prior damage to the
claimant's vehicle appears in our records or the inspection notes.
November 1, 2024
Claimant's counsel forwarded a medical report dsecribing a wrist fracture. The injury is plausible for a collision of this
type, and no earlier injury to the same area is on file.
November 7, 2024
Reviewed treatment records. Care followed a typical course, with the claimant's symptoms easing steadily as
recovery progressed and treatment tapering off accordingly.
November 15, 2024
Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account matched what the claimant told the intake
team and the treating clinic, and it has stayed consistent across every conversation.
December 11, 2024
The file does not make clear exactly where the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact. Requested
clarification from counsel and noted it as an open item for follow-up.
December 18, 2024
Nothing in the vehicle history or the policy records suggests the damage predates the coverage period. Reviewing the
claim against the documented facts, with the seating position as the one open question, before a settlement
recommendation is prepared.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
